## Introduction

In this seven-minute demonstration, we store versions of the
documented dataset and of a small model, then retrieve each by its
identifier. By the end, you should be able to explain how a version
identifier links a result to the exact input that produced it.

The pipeline in the hands-on activities reads a pinned dataset
version, so you prepared the board before the session. The instructor
runs the code below from the project root; the board and identifiers
in your MyBinder session are your own.
[Prepare the dataset versions](00_preparation.qmd#preparation-versions)

## Store dataset versions with pins

Allow about four minutes. A *pins* board stores named objects, called
pins. We use a local folder board with versioning enabled explicitly,
so each write adds a version instead of replacing the previous one.
We store the data as RDS, an R format that preserves the column types.

The prepared script writes two versions of the `health_wellbeing` pin.
The first contains all 29 studies, with the source URL and raw-file
checksum as metadata. The second contains the 18 general-population
studies. It is read from the exact full version, and its metadata
records the filter and that parent version. Rerunning the script
reuses identical versions instead of writing duplicates.

```{r health-versioning-prepare, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE, code = readLines(file.path("pipelines", "prepare_health_wellbeing.R"))}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show pipelines/prepare_health_wellbeing.R"
```

We open the same board and list its versions.

```{r health-versioning-board, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(
  pins[board_folder, pin_exists, pin_meta, pin_read, pin_versions],
  utils[read.csv]
)

workshop_dir <- file.path("outputs", "health-wellbeing")
data_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "data_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
pin_versions(data_board, "health_wellbeing")
```

The script also recorded which identifier belongs to which dataset.
We retrieve the subset's metadata and the full dataset by those
identifiers.

```{r health-versioning-read, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
versions <- read.csv(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv"),
  colClasses = "character"
)
full_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "all"]
general_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "general"]
stopifnot(length(full_version) == 1L, length(general_version) == 1L)

pin_meta(data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = general_version)$user

health_full <- pin_read(
  data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = full_version
)
nrow(health_full)
```

A version identifier names a stored object within this board. If you
recreate the board elsewhere, it receives new identifiers, so retain
the upstream checksum and the filter as well. In the hands-on
activities, the pipeline reads the version named in
`analysis-data-version.txt` rather than whichever version is newest.

## Store model versions with vetiver

Allow about three minutes. *vetiver* stores a fitted model on a pins
board together with what is needed to use it again: a *prototype* of
the expected inputs, the packages needed for prediction, and our own
metadata. Its standard interface supports common model types such as
`lm()`, but not the *meta* objects from our meta-analysis. We therefore
use a small supplementary predictive model.

The model predicts a study's Fisher-transformed correlation, `z`, from
its population type and the natural log of its sample size, `log_n`.
We store two versions under the same name: the second adds `log_n`.
Both regressions give each study equal weight and illustrate model
versioning only. The meta-analysis in the pipeline weights studies by
their precision and between-study variance.

```{r health-vetiver-setup, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(
  stats[lm],
  vetiver[vetiver_model, vetiver_pin_read, vetiver_pin_write]
)

original <- data.frame(
  population = factor(health_full$population),
  z = atanh(health_full$cor),
  log_n = log(health_full$n)
)

model_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "model_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
model_name <- "health_wellbeing"

model_source <- list(
  data_version = full_version,
  r_version = as.character(getRversion()),
  vetiver_version = as.character(utils::packageVersion("vetiver"))
)
```

Each render writes a new pair of model versions unless the cached
chunk below is reused. Cached chunks keep their recorded identifiers,
and the board keeps earlier versions. Keep the board with the
document cache; if you remove the board, refresh the cache when
rendering again.

```{r health-vetiver-versions, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE, cache.extra = get0("model_source")}
previous_versions <- if (pin_exists(model_board, model_name)) {
  pin_versions(model_board, model_name)$version
} else {
  character()
}

model_v1 <- lm(z ~ population, data = original)
v1 <- vetiver_model(
  model_v1,
  model_name = model_name,
  description = "Illustrative regression on population.",
  metadata = model_source
)
vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v1)
first_version <- setdiff(
  pin_versions(model_board, model_name)$version, previous_versions
)
stopifnot(length(first_version) == 1L)

model_v2 <- lm(z ~ population + log_n, data = original)
v2 <- vetiver_model(
  model_v2,
  model_name = model_name,
  description = "Illustrative regression on population and log sample size.",
  metadata = model_source
)
vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v2)

model_history <- pin_versions(model_board, model_name)
second_version <- setdiff(
  model_history$version, c(previous_versions, first_version)
)
stopifnot(length(second_version) == 1L)
c(first = first_version, second = second_version)
```

Without a version, `vetiver_pin_read()` selects the board's newest
version. Pass an explicit identifier to reproduce an earlier
prediction or inspect its input requirements.

```{r health-vetiver-read, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE, cache.extra = list(get0("first_version"), get0("second_version"))}
stored_v1 <- vetiver_pin_read(
  model_board, model_name, version = first_version
)
stored_v2 <- vetiver_pin_read(
  model_board, model_name, version = second_version
)
names(stored_v1$prototype)
names(stored_v2$prototype)
stored_v2$metadata$user
```

The model's metadata records its training data version and software
context [@vetiver-pin-write]. A model trained on restricted data can
reveal sensitive information, so keep fitted models local until you
have checked the applicable release terms. Creating a model API or
deploying a service is follow-up work.

## Checkpoint {#versioning-checkpoint}

- The data board lists two versions of `health_wellbeing`. The full
  version returns 29 rows, and the subset's metadata records its
  filter and parent version.
- The model board holds several versions under one name. The first
  model expects `population`; the second also expects `log_n`. Both
  record the dataset version they were trained on.
- You can explain why the pipeline reads a named version rather than
  the newest one.
